plan.name: Work a ratified plan of issues, one at a time
plan.summary: #112, which drafts and ratifies a PRD's plan of issues, isn't on the base branch yet, so this builds the watcher's side as `Factory.WorkPlan(ctx, PlanOfIssues)`, which is handed a ratified plan (the plan's issue, its hash, the writer who ratified it, the ratifying comment's URL, and its issues in order, each a `PlannedIssue` title and body) and runs within a poll or on its own; having each poll hand it the plans #112 ratifies is left for a follow-up once #112 merges. Each call answers each writer's `/invariant stop` on the plan's issue once, with a note; records any issue it opened for the plan and hasn't recorded; unless a writer has stopped the plan, opens the next issue once the one before it has merged, and records it; and once every issue has merged, says so, naming each: the records, which name their issue as #N, and that post go on the plan's issue as new kinds, `KindPlanOpened` and `KindPlanDone`, which, like notes, leave that issue's state as it was. It opens an issue through `CreateIssue`, which the GitHub interface gains as github.Client has it, the lease guards and the fake implements, with the step's title, no labels, and a body of the step's text without command lines, a line naming the plan's issue, the ratifier and the ratifying comment, and a hidden marker naming the plan's issue, hash and step; before opening one, it counts an open issue with that marker, opened by the factory's bot, or by a writer when there's no bot, as that step's, and an issue has merged once the factory's latest post on it says so or the pull request that post names has merged. Before each of those effects it describes the plan in `factory/plans`' terms as GitHub shows it, with this watcher holding the lease or not, and takes the effect only if the proved core's `Create`, `Record` or `Finish` allows it, refusing otherwise as a step outside the protocol is refused; go.mod requires that module, replaced by its directory, as it does factory/protocol. A new issue carrying such a marker is taken, as if the ratifier had written it with `/invariant solve`, only once the factory's own record on the plan's issue names it and while the ratifier can still write, and `stop` becomes a command that an issue's own step never answers and that never holds up the commands after it.

tests.name: TestAPlanOpensItsIssuesOneAtATime
tests.says: Handed a ratified plan of three issues, the watcher opens the first, titled as its step, with the step's text and a body naming the plan's issue and the ratifying comment, records it by number on the plan's issue, and takes it as the ratifier's; the second opens, and is recorded, only once the first has merged.

tests.name: TestACrashBetweenOpeningAndRecordingLeavesOneIssue
tests.says: A watcher that stops between opening an issue and recording it leaves one issue: nothing takes it until a fresh watcher finds it and records it without opening another, and then the watcher takes it.

tests.name: TestAnIssueClaimingAPlanIsntTakenOnItsAuthority
tests.says: As the App's bot, when a writer and a reader each open a copy of an issue the factory opened for a plan, before it's recorded and one numbered before it, a fresh watcher records only the factory's issue, and the copies are never drafted or posted on.

tests.name: TestNothingOpensAfterAStop
tests.says: After a writer's /invariant stop on the plan's issue, answered once, nothing more opens, even once the issue already open goes on to merge, and the plan isn't said to be done; a reader's stop changes nothing.

tests.name: TestThePlansIssueSaysWhenEveryIssueHasMerged
tests.says: Once the last of three issues has merged, here by a person whose merge closed the issue, the plan's issue says the plan is done, once, naming all three, and not before.
